paper.title_en: Influence of nuclear deformation on the <math><mi>α</mi></math>-decay systematics of superheavy nuclei with <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>130</mn></mrow></math>: Density-dependent cluster model and improved empirical approaches
paper.abstract_en: Systematic calculations of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-decay and spontaneous-fission (SF) properties are presented for the even-even superheavy isotopic chains with <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>130</mn></mrow></math>. The <math><mi>α</mi></math>-decay half-lives are evaluated within the density-dependent cluster model using a double-folding potential with a zero-range exchange approximation (DFM-ZR), employing the WS4 <math><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></math> values and deformation parameters <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> as inputs. The microscopic results are compared with the BKAG, UDL, NRDX, Horoi, and Ren A empirical formulas for both spherical and deformed daughter-nucleus configurations. To quantify the agreement between the microscopic and empirical predictions, the root-mean-square deviation, mean absolute deviation, and maximum absolute deviation of <math><mrow><msub><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mn>10</mn></msub><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> are evaluated for each isotopic chain. The calculations show that nuclear deformation has a significant influence on the <math><mi>α</mi></math>-decay systematics, particularly in the heavier chains where the daughter nuclei develop stronger prolate shapes. The DFM-ZR predictions exhibit trends similar to those of the BKAG, NRDX, Horoi, and Ren A formulas, whereas the UDL formula yields systematically shorter half-lives and larger deviations from the microscopic results. The predicted systematics further indicate a structural evolution from weakly deformed nuclei near the vicinity of the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>184</mn></mrow></math> shell closure to more pronounced prolate deformations at higher <math><mi>Z</mi></math>. Local irregularities around <math><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>194</mn></mrow></math> in the <math><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></math>, and half-life trends suggest a possible deformed subshell effect, although a more detailed shell-structure analysis would be required to confirm this interpretation. Comparison with the SF half-lives shows that spontaneous fission becomes increasingly competitive with increasing proton number and is predicted to dominate for many nuclei with <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>126</mn></mrow></math>, whereas the <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>124</mn></mrow></math> chains remain more favorable candidates for observable <math><mi>α</mi></math> decay. These results provide a consistent theoretical framework and useful guidance for future searches for superheavy nuclei beyond the presently known limit of the nuclear chart.
